summary: Jackson County, OR lookout on Ragsdale Butte: rag camp 1933, L-4 cab 1939, removed, destroyed or burned 1962-63; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: Rag camp (1933), later an L-4 cab (1939)
facts.status_note: Cab removed, destroyed or burned in 1962-63; the sources disagree on the year and the manner. No source describes the site now.
facts.agency: Oregon Dept. of Forestry (per the register); Forest Lookouts files the site under Umpqua National Forest

events.note: Rag camp set up on the north summit, per the register; firelookout.com calls it a camp
September 1933 paper says the CCC would build a 10x10 lookout before snow; no source says it was built
Road crew at work building the road to Ragsdale Peak lookout, per the Medford Mail Tribune
L-4 cab replaced the rag camp
Bob Mooney given the position of lookout man, per the Medford Mail Tribune
Register says the L-4 cab was removed around 1962
Forest Lookouts says the lookout burned by the Forest Service in 1963

evidence.supports: rag camp set up on north summit in 1933, replaced in 1939 with an L-4 cab, cab removed around 1962
evidence.quote: Set up atop the north summit in 1933, a rag camp was replaced in 1939 with an L-4 cab, which was removed around 1962.

evidence.supports: September 1933 paper says the CCC is to build a 10x10 lookout before the snow flies
evidence.quote: A 10x10 lookout is to be constructed by the CCC before the snow flies.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts heads the entry Umpqua National Forest
administered by Oregon Dept. of Forestry
May 1934: Rogue River National Forest road superintendent reports a road crew at work toward Ragsdale Peak lookout
evidence.quote: Bill Jones, road superintendent for the Rogue River national forest

evidence.supports: road crew at work on the construction to Ragsdale Peak lookout
evidence.quote: A road crew is now at work on the construction to Ragsdale Peak lookout.

evidence.supports: May 1941: Bob Mooney given the position of lookout man, to take up the work within days
evidence.quote: Bob Mooney has the position of lookout man at the Ragsdale Butte lookout station and will take up the work within a few days.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts: 1963 the lookout burned by the Forest Service
evidence.quote: 1963: The lookout burned by the Forest Service.

evidence.supports: 2007 photo labelled as the lookout site in the register; caption gives no further description
evidence.quote: Ragsdale Butte Lookout site 2007 - courtesy of Ron Kemnow

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the L-4 cab was removed around 1962 and firelookout.com says destroyed 1962; the Forest Lookouts page gives 1963 and says it burned. The story gives both dates and does not pick one.

The register lists the Oregon Department of Forestry as administrator. The Forest Lookouts page heads the entry Umpqua National Forest, and its 1934 item refers to the Rogue River National Forest road superintendent. The brief's agency value is kept, and the story says the sources disagree.

The register and firelookout.com describe a 1933 rag camp or camp. A September 1933 paper says the CCC would build a 10x10 lookout before snow. No source confirms that the 10x10 lookout was built, so it is reported only as a plan.

notes_for_editor: Brief record kept: status gone, agency Oregon Dept. of Forestry, with the forest-attribution conflict recorded. Access is unknown in every source read, so no access fact is written. A Kemnow PDF copy of the Forest Lookouts page at orww.org carries the same entries (the 1941 quote is split across lines there), so the weebly page is cited. Two web searches found nothing describing the site today.
